name: Dumah
overview: Dumah is a male figure identified as the sixth-born son of Ishmael, belonging to the tribe named after him. The biblical record provides limited information about him beyond his lineage and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Dumah means "silence" in Hebrew. This proper name, recorded in Genesis 25:14, was not given by God but is the personal name by which he is known in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Dumah is explicitly identified as a son of Ishmael, making him part of the Ishmaelite lineage. Scripture does not record any additional family relationships for Dumah beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Dumah's significance in the biblical narrative stems primarily from his position as a son of Ishmael, through whom the Ishmaelite tribes are traced. His mention in Genesis situates him within the broader story of God's covenantal dealings with Abraham's descendants, highlighting the expansion of Ishmael's lineage.
